name: Kuntaka
dates_notes: Kuntaka is generally placed in the tenth century by relative position in the history of Sanskrit poetics. Secure biographical data are unavailable.
core_thesis: Kuntaka makes *vakrokti*, oblique or distinctive expression, the principle that animates poetry. Poetic force arises when language departs from ordinary expression in structured ways, from phonetic patterning through word choice and sentence formation to the organization of an entire composition. This is neither a simple catalogue of ornaments nor a denial of rasa or suggestion; it is a theory of literary originality that locates aesthetic value in patterned deviation across multiple levels of language.

engaged_works.title: Vakrokti-Jivita
engaged_works.composition_dates_notes: Usually assigned to the tenth century by relative textual chronology.
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The extant poetics treatise is securely transmitted as Kuntaka's work.

ascription_evidence.description: Modern histories of Sanskrit poetics treat the Vakrokti-Jīvita as Kuntaka's work.

engaged_works.summary: A Sanskrit treatise on poetic obliqueness, traditionally organized in four sections. It distinguishes forms of vakrokti at several linguistic and compositional levels, including sound, word, sentence, episode, and whole work. The text gives a systematic account of why expressive deviation can be aesthetically significant.
